name: APPSC Group-I Services
department: Government of Andhra Pradesh (Revenue, Police, State Tax, Education, Panchayat Raj and other departments)
summary: Andhra Pradesh's top state service exam: Deputy Collector, DSP, Assistant Commissioner of State Tax, District Educational Officer, Divisional Development Officer and more. Objective Screening test, five descriptive Main papers plus qualifying Telugu and English, and a 75-mark interview (825 marks in all).

status.note: Notification 07/2026 (166 posts) is open: applications 6 to 27 October 2026; Screening test on 24 January 2027; Main exam dates to be announced.

posts.name: Deputy Collector (A.P. Civil Service, Executive)
posts.responsibilities: Revenue Divisional Officer and district administration; can rise to IAS by conferment.

posts.name: Deputy Superintendent of Police (Civil) Cat-2
posts.notes: 36 posts (3 carried forward). Age 21 to 30; physical standards apply.

posts.name: District Educational Officer
posts.responsibilities: Heads school education in a district.

posts.name: Assistant Treasury Officer / Assistant Accounts Officer

relaxations.note: Based on service, as per notification.
Plus length of service, as per notification.

age.summary: Minimum 18 (21 for DSP Civil) and maximum 44 (30 for DSP posts) on 1 July 2026, under Rule 12 of the APS&SS Rules 1996 read with G.O.Ms.No.187 and 188 GA (Ser-A) of 14 Sep 2026.
age.referenceDate: 1 July of the notification year (1 Jul 2026)

eligibility.domicile: Local status under the AP local cadre rules matters for zonal and multi-zonal reservation; non-locals can compete for open, non-local quotas as per rules.

education.summary: A bachelor's degree from a recognised university for most posts; some posts specify subjects or preferences (see the notification).

eligibility.physical: DSP posts have physical and medical standards (Annexure V).
eligibility.examVsPost: One exam, 13 kinds of posts with different age limits (DSP 30, others 44). You give post and multi-zone or zone preferences online before Mains and again at certificate verification; preferences at verification are mandatory.
disqualifications: Absence in any Screening or Main paper disqualifies the candidate.
eligibility.reservation: Andhra Pradesh rules: SC 15% (sub-categorised into groups as per the 2025 orders, applied as stated in the notification), ST 6%, BC 29% (A 7%, B 10%, C 1%, D 7%, E 4%), EWS 10%. Horizontal reservation for women (33 1/3%), PwBD, ex-servicemen and sportspersons. Local, zonal and multi-zonal reservation under the AP Presidential Order and local cadre rules.

eligibilityRules.notes: DSP posts: 21 (Civil) to 30. Age relaxation for SC, ST, BC and EWS is 5 years.

stages.name: Screening test (objective, OMR)

papers.name: Paper I: General Studies (history and culture; constitution, polity, social justice, IR; Indian and AP economy and planning; geography)
Paper II: General Aptitude (mental ability, administrative and psychological abilities; science and technology; current events)

stages.notes: Shortlists 50 times the vacancies for Mains, irrespective of community. Relaxed standards may be applied for SC, ST, BC and PwBD to fill reserved vacancies.

stages.name: Main exam (descriptive)

papers.name: Paper II: History, Culture and Geography of India and AP
Paper III: Polity, Constitution, Governance, Law and Ethics
Paper IV: Economy and Development of India and AP
Paper V: Science, Technology and Environmental Issues

stages.notes: All papers are compulsory; absence in any paper disqualifies.

selection.meritCalculation: Final merit = Main written (5 papers, 750) + interview (75) = 825. Minimum aggregate: OC, sportspersons and EWS 40%; BC 35%; SC, ST and PwBD 30%.
selection.tieBreaking: Equal Mains totals are bracketed and ranked by age (oldest first); then by the earlier date of qualification. Where a preferential qualification is prescribed, it takes priority over age.
selection.languages: Main exam medium option (English or Telugu, as offered) is taken online before Mains.
selection.documentVerification: Before final selection, with post and zone preferences.
selection.probation: As per AP State and Subordinate Service Rules.

supplementary: AP-specific history, economy and policy carry heavy weight in both stages.
The full syllabus is in Annexure II of the notification.

sections.subject: Paper I: General Studies (degree standard)
topics: History and culture: Indus Valley to modern India, including AP history
Constitution, polity, social justice and international relations
Indian and Andhra Pradesh economy and planning

sections.subject: Paper II: General Aptitude
topics: General mental ability, administrative and psychological abilities
Current events of regional, national and international importance

sections.subject: Five merit papers
topics: History, culture and geography of India and AP
Polity, constitution, governance, law and ethics
Economy and development of India and AP

rankAndAllocation.text: Candidates are selected in merit order against post and zone preferences, applying community, local and horizontal reservations. Carried-forward reserved vacancies are filled first.

salary.pension: Contributory Pension Scheme for those joining after 1 Sep 2004.
salary.notes: Starting basic shown is Deputy Collector / DSP / ACST (61,960-1,51,370). DDO starts at 65,360; Municipal Commissioner Gr-II and others at 54,060.

progression.post: Special Grade Deputy Collector / Joint Collector cadre
IAS (by conferment from state civil service)

career.promotionNotes: State civil service officers can be appointed to the IAS by promotion through the UPSC select list after many years of service. DSPs can be promoted to IPS similarly.
career.macp: Automatic Advancement Scheme as per AP rules.

benefits.detail: HRA or quarters, medical (EHS), leave and LTC as per AP rules.

workLife.postings: Anywhere in Andhra Pradesh by zone and multi-zone.

difficulty.rationale: Five descriptive papers and an interview for only 166 posts; earlier Group-I cycles drew lakhs of applicants.

ratings.rationale: Top state posts with a path to IAS/IPS, but notifications are irregular.

factors.note: Group-I is notified every few years.
Earlier AP Group-I recruitments were challenged in court and delayed.
Notification to final result usually takes 1 to 2 years.

sections.title: How AP Group-I works
paragraphs: Three stages. The Screening test (two objective papers of 120 marks) only shortlists, about 50 candidates per vacancy. Mains has five descriptive papers of 150 marks each plus two qualifying language papers (Telugu and English). The interview carries 75 marks.

sections.title: Minimum marks and ties
paragraphs: To be selected you must reach the minimum aggregate for your category. If totals are equal, the older candidate ranks higher.

sections.title: Common confusions
bullets: DSP posts have a lower upper age (30) and physical standards; other posts allow up to 44.
The Screening test marks are not added to your final score.
You must give post and zone preferences at certificate verification even if you gave them before Mains.

gaps: Official cutoffs and applicant counts for earlier cycles not collected.
